title: As a platform engineer, infrastructure is code on day one — a first-party IaC surface (templates plus a typed CDK-style framework) with documented state/rollback semantics
As a platform engineer, the official Terraform/OpenTofu provider is real — vendor-maintained, actively released, covering the core services I run
As a platform engineer, existing resources can come under IaC — documented import/drift workflows instead of a greenfield-only story
As a security engineer, least privilege is expressible — fine-grained IAM policies with conditions, resource-level scoping, and documented policy evaluation
As a security engineer, nothing ships a long-lived key — OIDC/workload identity federation issues short-lived credentials to CI and services, documented end to end
As an AI-native team, agents get their own leash — documented patterns for handing an agent temporary, narrowly-scoped credentials it cannot escalate
As a founder, the bill cannot silently explode — budgets, alerts, and documented anomaly detection on spend, configurable from day one
As an analyst, cost data is queryable — a billing/cost API and scheduled exports with resource-level granularity, not just a dashboard screenshot
As a founder, prices are published — public per-service pricing pages and an official calculator I can estimate a stack with before signing anything
As a founder, starting is free — an always-free tier and/or published startup credits with the limits and expiry spelled out
As a developer, experiments cannot hurt prod — documented multi-account/project isolation patterns (org units, sandboxes) with guardrails
As a developer, first deploy is under an hour — official quickstarts that go from zero to a running service with the exact commands shown
As a platform engineer, Kubernetes is managed — a first-party managed K8s service with documented upgrade policy and autoscaling
As a developer, small services need no servers — first-party functions/serverless containers with documented triggers, limits, and cold-start behavior
As a developer, the database is a service — managed relational offerings with automated backups, HA options, and documented maintenance windows
As an operations lead, I can pick where things run — a published region list with per-region service availability I can check before committing
As a developer, every service has a real reference — consistent API/CLI reference docs across the platform, not just the flagship services
As an operations lead, outages are owned in public — a real status/health surface with per-service history and post-incident reports
As an AI-native team, models are a platform service — first-party managed inference over frontier and open models with a documented API
As an AI-native team, agents have a managed home — first-party agent runtimes/orchestration services shipped and documented, not just a blog vision
